notes: scan045.N1: The introduction proposes later sheafification over X and later passage from a topological space to an arbitrary topos. It postpones connectivity/local connectivity conditions and says that normal local triviality of embeddings is not needed at this stage. This mathematical narrative was carried as background while reading, not proved.

scan045.N2: The lower block introduces an ordered index set I and a locally finite family of closed subspaces X_i with i≤j implying X_i⊂X_j. Formula (2) writes X_{Delta_0} as a coproduct and as a set of pairs; the local second coordinate in the pair remains palaeographically doubtful. These written assertions were carried as background without an independent proof.

scan045.N3: Twenty-three main written lines were read, counting the two heading lines and each display row. The two raised insertion tiers and both marginal number positions were also read. Every body word and symbol was compared with both witnesses, including their agreements. The whole-page image was read once after an earlier tool delivery had been truncated before visual inspection; each supplied half and each of the thirteen saved crops was then visually inspected once. No OCR, external research, other-page image, other reader report or TeX compilation was used.

scan045.N4: Literal grammatical irregularities are retained: relatifs and faisceautisés are masculine in the written sentence whose subject is constructions. The opening quote before faisceautisés has no corresponding closing mark on this page. No closing quotation or gender correction is supplied.

scan045.N5: The dark 10 at the top is treated as the author page number. The pale bottom-left 44 is another hand’s foliation and is encoded with margin, not mspage. The heading 2 and 1/2, display labels 1, 1′ and 2, and the subscript 0 in Delta_0 are all covered by audit boxes.
scan045.N6: The page ends with the unpunctuated phrase on a un morphisme canonique. No morphism is completed on this page. There is no figure or diagram and no footnote.

scan045.N7: There are two distinct deletions and two distinct insertions: the cancelled mathematical group after ordonné; the cancelled word below (1); alors linked after amènera; and sous-espaces placed above the cancelled word. Each is separately inventoried. The underlines in the heading and the leader for alors are not treated as cancellations.

scan045.N8: Both supplied marks are resolved to their first readings. The unlisted C doubt in the cancelled mathematical group is retained. Three additional certainty qualifications are added: the compressed preposition/punctuation mark, the buried letters of parties, and the overtraced pair coordinate in (2). These do not count as secure textual corrections to C.

scan045.N9: The live X_i before the inclusion in (1) has heavy retracing and top/bottom serif-like strokes. Its crossed X body and separate dotted subscript remain readable. No earlier letter or extra deletion is inferred. Formula (1′) preserves a double-shaft implication arrow, subset signs without a lower equality bar, a comma after fermés, and the two final periods.

scan045.N10. First-pass accounting, retained as history; the final reconciled totals are in the changes summary and this report’s counts object. Compiler-facing counts follow the diff_c/diff_h flags. Seventeen report entries contain fourteen H disagreements and zero C disagreements: thirteen H disagreements have high-confidence ink evidence, and the cancelled X_i versus H ill is one explicitly tentative disagreement, not a secure recovery. The actual handwritten 10 and 44 omitted by H and the three quotation-form differences are included. The three certainty-only rows r03, r10 and r12 are not counted as textual disagreements. Changing the provenance macro for C’s correctly read 44 is not a C fault.

scan045.N11: All eleven token differences in the blind reading were inspected on their saved crops. The first reading stands, including the half sign in the heading, amènera with raised alors, normale, seront and faisceautisés. The old indexed group and the retraced pair coordinate retain their existing doubts; no new deletion or overbar is inferred from retracing.
